n: David asks God to hear his complaint and guard his life from the dread his enemies cause.

f.g: Here, “complaint” — an honest lament poured out to God.

n: He asks to be hidden from the secret plots and noisy mob of evildoers.
Their tongues are sharpened like swords, and their cruel words fly like arrows.
From hiding they shoot at the innocent without warning and without any fear of consequence.

f.g: The blameless, the person of integrity.

n: They egg each other on, plan hidden traps, and ask, “Who will ever see?”
They work hard devising perfect crimes. Human hearts and minds are deep — and capable of great cunning.
The great reversal: God himself shoots an arrow, and they are suddenly struck — just as they tried to strike the innocent.

f.g: The same words as verse 4, turned back on the attackers.

n: Their own tongues bring them down, and onlookers shake their heads and back away.

f.w: make their own tongue to fall upon themselves

n: Everyone will be struck with awe, tell what God has done, and think carefully about it.
The righteous will rejoice, take refuge in the Lord, and celebrate.
